To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the relationship between intervention scale and performance is non-linear and U-shaped: small-scale interventions have positive effect on performance, whereas large-scale interventions are counter-productive.

(1) large scale interventions are effective in the start up phase of systems (new products, companies, markets, etc.); (2) large scale interventions have a counter-productive effect in mature systems (e.g., companies in a mature industry); (3) small scale interventions are generally ineffective in the start-up and mature phase; (4) small scale interventions have a positive impact in mature systems; and (5) small scale interventions can be effective in the early stages of the start

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the more complex the system the more the need to understand its dynamics, and to intervene at the appropriate scale.
the more complex the organization the less the need for intervention, and the less complex the organization the more the need for intervention.

the relationship between scale and performance is not linear, but rather exhibits a non-linear pattern.
decision-makers need to be mindful of the scale of their intervention in order to avoid the common tendency to ‘over intervene’ in the systems they manage.
managers and leaders must learn how to manage the scale of their actions in order to avoid counter-productive interventions.
